provenance.paper_title: StreamFlow: Dynamic Memory Flows for Streaming Video Understanding

evidence.paraphrase: A lightweight mid-term memory filters temporal redundancy before full visual encoding.

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Historical content is consolidated into visual latents and injected by attention-guided retrieval.
During operation, StreamFlow applies fixed-rule insertion or replacement to dynamics-aware mid-term visual memory; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.
Redundant streaming observations are filtered before encoding. For StreamFlow, this specifically supports merging or deduplication of overlapping entries of dynamics-aware mid-term visual memory.
Mid-term content is consolidated into long-term visual latents. For StreamFlow, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of dynamics-aware mid-term visual memory.

derived.hybrid_relation: Distinct operative representation paths are explicitly linked for downstream retrieval, reasoning, or control.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): During inference, the operative memory component (dynamics-aware mid-term visual memory) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries, episodic or hierarchical summarization; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
